title: Erasure, and the webhook that proves it
summary: The right to be forgotten across systems: the vault wipes every scope's copy, then tells each scope's own system to forget its pseudonym - over a signed callback that lands in the inbox below.

steps.label: A record to erase
steps.note: Registered by the CRM, like any other customer.

steps.label: The data is there
steps.note: One field read, so the difference after the erasure is visible rather than asserted.

steps.label: The privacy officer sees every scope that holds them
steps.note: Right of access is org-wide and linkage-capable, which is why it is a separate, high-privilege action held by one client - not something the support desk can call.

steps.label: Erase the person
steps.note: One transaction: every scope's encrypted blob and every identifier token is wiped, outstanding one-time identifiers die with them, and one erasure event per scope is queued for delivery. The audit chain keeps the fact of the erasure - the evidence must outlive the data.

steps.label: The field is gone
steps.note: Not masked, not flagged as deleted: the ciphertext is gone, so there is nothing left to decrypt.

steps.label: And so is the way to find them
steps.note: The search tokens went with the record: a lookup by the same phone number is now a plain miss.
